questions.question: Which of the following novels is written by Mulk Raj Anand that shows the cruelty of the caste system based on pre-independence era of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Untouchable.__**

questions.question: Which organisation was created in 1988 by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) and the United Nations Environment Program (UNEP) to assess the science related to climate change ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC).__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)** was established by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) in 1988.
 
• The establishment of the IPCC was endorsed by UN General Assembly in 1988.
 
• The IPCC was set up in 1988 by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) and United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) to **provide policymakers with regular assessments of the scientific basis of climate change, its impacts, future risks, and options for adaptation and mitigation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Climate Action Network (CAN) is a global network of more than 1,800 civil society organizations in over 130 countries driving collective and sustainable action to fight the climate crisis and to achieve social and racial justice.
 
• International Climate Action Network (I-CAN) is a 30-month Erasmus+ funded international project to give teachers the skills, confidence, and framework to enable pupils to become effective critical thinking collaborators and active climate-conscious.
 
• The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is a treaty-based inter-governmental international development organization headquartered in Seoul, South Korea.
 
• The Australian Youth Climate Coalition is a youth organization in Australia.
 
• When the organisation first began, the coalition consisted of 25 other youth organisations, which included the National Union of Students amongst many, however, it is now an independent organization.

questions.question: DDT adversely affects our environment because:

options.text: it can kill beneficial insects like honey bees
it can allow growth of harmful insects
it can promote growth of harmful insects

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**it can kill beneficial insects like honey bees.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• DDT is **very insoluble in water and very persistent in the environment, making it a highly polluting hazard**.
 
• Its half-life has been reported to be between **2 and 15 years.**
 
• DDT (dichloro-diphenyl-trichloroethane) was developed as the first of the **modern synthetic insecticides** in the 1940s.
 
• It was initially used with great effect to **combat malaria, typhus, and other insect-borne human diseases among both military and civilian populations**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Insecticides are **chemicals used to control insects by killing them or preventing them from engaging in undesirable or destructive behaviours**.
 
• Organic pesticides are usually considered as those **pesticides that come from natural sources**. 
 
• Synthetic** contact insecticides** are now the **primary agents of insect control**.​ 
 
• Inorganic insecticides are **of mineral origin, mainly compounds of antimony, arsenic, barium, boron, copper, fluorine, mercury, selenium, sulfur, thallium, and zinc, and elemental phosphorus and sulfur**.

questions.question: Which unicellular organism acquires food by a process in which cells absorb external material by engulfing it with the cell membrane?

__
 
• In **Amoeba**, the cell membrane help in** engulfing the food **during the process called **endocytosis.**

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Padma Subrahmanyam** (born 4 February 1943, in Madras), is an Indian classical **Bharata Natyam dancer.**
 
• She is also a research** scholar, choreographer, teacher, Indologist, and author.**
 
• She received the honours of Padma Shri in 1981 and Padma Bhushan in 2003.
 
• She is **famous in India too abroad;** several films and documentaries have been made in her honour by countries such as Japan, Australia, and Russia.
 
• She is famous as the **developer and founder** of the dance form **Bharata Nrithyam.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Savitha Sastry** is an Indian dancer and choreographer best known as an exponent of **Bharatanatyam**.​ 
 
• **Mallika Sarabhai** is an activist and Indian classical dancer and actress from Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India.
 
• **Rukmini Devi Arundale** was an Indian** theosophist, dancer, and choreographer** of the Indian classical dance form of Bharatanatyam, and an activist for animal welfare.

questions.question: Mallika Sarabhai, a Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam dancer, was awarded with the Padma Bhushan in which of the following years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2010.**__

__
 
• Mallika Sarabhai Padma Bhushan Awarded In **2010.**
 
• Daughter of a classical dancer** Mrinalini Sarabhai and renowned space scientist Vikram Sarabhai, **Mallika is an accomplished **Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam** dancer and performer.
 
• Mallika Sarabhai has been honored with several awards.
 
• Mallika Sarabhai (born 9 May 1954) is an activist and Indian **classical dancer and actress** from Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India.

• **​****The Padma Vibhushan** is the **second-highest civilian award** of the Republic of India, after the Bharat Ratna. 
 
• Instituted on 2 January 1954, the award is given for** "exceptional and distinguished service".**
 
• All persons without distinction of** race, occupation, position or sex **are eligible for these awards.

questions.question: _______ of the Constitution of India provides protection against arrest and detention in certain cases.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 22.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 22** of the Indian Constitution **provides protection against such arrest and detention inserted **in cases in preventive detention under** Section 151** of the Criminal Procedure Code** 1973.**
 
• Preventive detention is without trial. A person can be detained only on grounds of suspicion hence the rights of a person arrested in this manner get governed by preventive detention laws.
 
• Preventive detention is an action taken on grounds of suspicion some wrong actions may be done by the person concerned hence a **Police officer can arrest an individual without orders from a magistrate without a warrant **if he gets any information of such an individual cannot commit any offence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​Article 25 guarantees the freedom of conscience, the freedom to profess, practice, and propagate religion to all citizens.
 
• **Article 23** in the Constitution Of India 1949 means **Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour**. 
 
• **The Right against Exploitation is enshrined in Articles 23 and 24 of the Indian Constitution**. 
 
• **Article 20**, no person shall be convicted of any offense except for violation of the law in force at the time of the commission of the act charged as an offence, nor be subjected to a penalty greater than that which might have been inflicted under the law in force at the time of the commission of the offence.
